That is a position, not a motive. This is only my impression: remedies that touch big money face a higher bar of proof among such thinkers than other ideas do.

Some of that bar is sound. [Chesterton's fence](../mind/famous-lessons.md) says not to tear down what you do not understand, and rocking the boat of a working economy can make things far worse. Some of it is ordinary bias. Psychologists call the pull toward the existing state of affairs [status quo bias](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Status_quo_bias), and the urge to defend existing arrangements [system justification](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/System_justification).

I am not wise enough to draw the exact line between the two. What I can say is that timing matters. In February 1933, [25 German industrialists](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Secret_Meeting_of_20_February_1933) met Hitler and gave about two million Reichsmarks to his campaign. I wonder how that year would have gone if more people of their standing had said no. [Dwight Eisenhower](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dwight_D._Eisenhower%27s_farewell_address), a general and no radical, did speak up on his way out, warning against "unwarranted influence" by the "military-industrial complex". [Who We Thank](who-we-thank.md) follows that warning to the ballpark.

So those who respect the fence still ought to speak a little louder when the moment looks consequential. That asks public thinkers to read a crystal ball, which may not be fair. But I agree with [Chomsky](../mind/chomsky.md) that [intellectuals](https://en.wikiquote.org/wiki/Noam_Chomsky) "are in a position to expose the lies of governments", and that the position carries a duty. I would only ask for more diplomacy than he usually shows.

==== Confederate Monuments (Society) https://que.one/society/monuments.html
Kind: take

## Confederate Monuments

[Confederate monuments](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Confederate_monuments_and_memorials) were mostly raised decades after the Civil War, many during the Jim Crow era. They present the Confederacy through the [Lost Cause](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lost_Cause_of_the_Confederacy) story rather than through the historical record of [slavery in the United States](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Slavery_in_the_United_States). These monuments and flags honor a myth. The myth helps people forget the larger context and ugliness of slavery rather than remember it. As the documentary maker [Ken Burns](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ken_Burns) has put it, they represent stories, not facts. They are myths I do not think we should cherish.

==== Not Conservatism (Society) https://que.one/society/not-conservatism.html
Kind: note

## Not Conservatism

The strongest case against this administration does not need liberal arguments. It comes from conservative ones: the Constitution, institutional restraint, and the rule of law, the values I swore to uphold when I served. Measured by those, this is not conservative governance. It is institutional decay.

[Rule of Law](rule-of-law.md) covers the Justice Department and the pardons. Four more failures should trouble any conservative.

The first is civilian control of an apolitical military. Six Democratic lawmakers, all veterans or former security officials, reminded troops that they [can refuse illegal orders](https://www.npr.org/2025/11/24/nx-s1-5619314/pentagon-mark-kelly-trump-hegseth-military). The president answered "SEDITIOUS BEHAVIOR, punishable by DEATH!" and the Pentagon moved to punish Senator Mark Kelly.

A federal judge [blocked](https://www.npr.org/2026/02/12/nx-s1-5698515/mark-kelly-pete-hegseth-lawsuit) the censure on First Amendment grounds. Refusing an illegal order is not sedition. It is the oath.

The second is free speech. In September 2025 ABC [suspended](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Suspension_of_Jimmy_Kimmel_Live%21) Jimmy Kimmel. The chairman of the Federal Communications Commission had just warned broadcasters they could do this "the easy way or the hard way." Satire is a pressure valve of a free society. Silencing it is insecurity dressed up as power.

The third is honest numbers and free trade. The president [fired](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Erika_McEntarfer) the head of the Bureau of Labor Statistics after a weak jobs report. The New York Fed [found](https://libertystreeteconomics.newyorkfed.org/2026/02/who-is-paying-for-the-2025-u-s-tariffs/) that Americans paid most of his tariffs. Both used to be conservative principles.

The fourth is the war power. The Constitution gives it to Congress. Yet Congress never [authorized](https://www.npr.org/2026/01/14/g-s1-106093/senate-war-powers-venezuela) the strikes on alleged drug boats or the January 2026 raid on Caracas that seized Nicolás Maduro. The war on Iran began on February 28, 2026, and Congress has [never voted](https://www.npr.org/2026/09/24/nx-s1-5980318/senate-iran-war-powers-vote) to authorize that either. In polls since it began, most Americans have [opposed it](https://www.npr.org/2026/03/06/nx-s1-5737627/iran-us-military-poll-trump-approval).

Even former loyalists broke ranks: [Marjorie Taylor Greene](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Marjorie_Taylor_Greene) opposed it, and [Joe Kent](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Joe_Kent) resigned as the nation's counterterrorism chief over it. A war most citizens oppose and their representatives never approved is exactly the unchecked power conservatives used to warn against.

These trends corrode the habits and restraints that make self-government possible.

==== Oligarchy (Society) https://que.one/society/oligarchy.html
Kind: note

## Oligarchy

An [oligarchy](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Oligarchy) is rule by a few, and in practice by the few who are rich. It is tempting to pin the state of U.S. politics on [Donald Trump](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Donald_Trump) alone. In my reading he is the face, and the lasting force is concentrated wealth that shapes the law. The test is to look at who gains and who pays.

Take the [tax and spending law](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/One_Big_Beautiful_Bill_Act) he signed in July 2025. The [Congressional Budget Office](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Congressional_Budget_Office) (CBO), the nonpartisan scorekeeper of Congress, [estimates](https://www.cbo.gov/publication/61461) that it adds $3.4 trillion to deficits through 2034, or [$4.1 trillion](https://www.crfb.org/blogs/whats-one-big-beautiful-bill-act) with interest. CBO's [household analysis](https://www.cbo.gov/publication/61469) of August 2025 shows where the money goes. The poorest tenth of households lose about $1,200 a year, mostly through cuts to Medicaid and food aid. The richest tenth gain about [$13,600](https://tax.thomsonreuters.com/news/cbo-analyzes-distributional-effects-of-budget-act/) a year.

The pattern is older than that law. In his first term Trump approved [$8.4 trillion](https://www.crfb.org/papers/trump-and-biden-national-debt) of new ten-year borrowing, against $4.3 trillion under Joe Biden through mid-2024. Most of it was bipartisan, which is part of the point. The largest partisan item was the [2017 tax cut](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tax_Cuts_and_Jobs_Act), at $1.9 trillion.

Now follow the campaign money. One hundred billionaire families spent [$2.6 billion](https://americansfortaxfairness.org/billionaires-buying-elections-theyve-come-to-collect/) on the 2024 federal elections, one dollar in every six. [Elon Musk](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Elon_Musk) alone spent more than [$290 million](https://www.cnn.com/2025/02/01/politics/elon-musk-2024-election-spending-millions), then became the de facto leader of the new administration's [cost-cutting office](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Department_of_Government_Efficiency). Yet Forbes counted [more billionaires](https://fortune.com/2024/10/23/billioniares-back-harris-more-than-trump-musk-cuban/) behind Kamala Harris than behind Trump, 81 to 51. The money sits on both sides, which is why removing one man would not fix it. Biden himself [warned](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Joe_Biden%27s_farewell_address) on leaving office that an oligarchy was taking hold.

The [Federal Reserve](https://www.federalreserve.gov/releases/z1/dataviz/dfa/distribute/table/) shows the result. By mid-2026 the top 1% held 32.5% of the nation's household wealth, and the bottom half held 2.3%.

Supporters answer that growth and tariffs cover the cost. CBO's growth-adjusted estimate came out [higher](https://www.crfb.org/blogs/obbba-dynamic-score-comes-47-trillion), not lower, because more borrowing raises interest rates. The Supreme Court [struck down](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Learning_Resources,_Inc._v._Trump) the emergency tariffs in February 2026, and CBO now projects a [$2.1 trillion](https://fortune.com/2026/08/10/how-big-deficit-national-debt-tariffs-cbo/) deficit for fiscal 2026.

Whether "oligarchy" is the right word is still [argued](https://journals.sagepub.com/doi/10.1177/2053168015608896) among political scientists. The ledger is not. [Identity](us-identity-politics.md) sells the story, and money writes the law. [Markets](markets-capitalism.md) are tools, so the remedy is [rules](rule-of-law.md), not a change of face.

CBO's site turns away automated requests, so each CBO figure here also carries a second source.

==== The Orbán Playbook (Society) https://que.one/society/orban-playbook.html
Kind: note

## The Orbán Playbook

What worries me about American institutions is the method more than any single act. [Viktor Orbán](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Viktor_Orb%C3%A1n) showed how it works in Hungary. His party turned 53% of the vote in 2010 into two-thirds of the seats. It then passed a new constitution after nine days of debate and reshaped the courts, all by legal means. Elections kept happening, on a tilted field. Scholars call this [competitive authoritarianism](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Competitive_authoritarianism).

I am not the first to see the pattern here. [Steven Levitsky](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Steven_Levitsky) and [Lucan Way](https://munkschool.utoronto.ca/person/lucan-way), who named it, [argue](https://www.npr.org/2026/05/13/nx-s1-5816313/word-of-week-competitive-authoritarianism) that the United States has slid into it. [Garry Kasparov](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Garry_Kasparov) has [long drawn the same line](https://www.kasparov.com/putin-and-trump-share-an-authoritarian-spirit-kasparov/) to Putin. At home I see a [measurable decline](rule-of-law.md) in the rule of law and corruption excused as strength. I also see a Congress that has largely stopped checking Donald Trump.

The tilt reaches elections too. A 2025 executive order demanded proof of citizenship to register until courts [blocked it](https://www.pbs.org/newshour/politics/federal-judge-bars-trump-from-implementing-proof-of-citizenship-requirement-to-vote), and Texas [redrew its districts](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2025_Texas_redistricting) in mid-decade at the president's urging.

Fear makes the playbook work. [Karen Stenner](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Karen_Stenner) found that perceived threats push people with an authoritarian streak toward intolerance and deference. People frightened of exaggerated threats outsource their courage to a strongman, excuse cruelty, and accept intimidation, as long as they feel safe.

The United States is not Hungary. Its courts still rule against the president, and its states run their own elections. The playbook can also be beaten. Given a fair enough chance, voters end it: in 2026 Hungarians [voted Orbán out](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2026_Hungarian_parliamentary_election) after 16 years.

For Dominicans who lived under [Rafael Trujillo](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rafael_Trujillo#Rise_to_power), his is still the name that lands. He never needed a single blow either. In 1930 he kept the army in its barracks while a revolt toppled the president, then won a rigged election.

Institutions rarely fall at once. They fall when the people meant to defend them stand aside.

==== The Perception Gap (Society) https://que.one/society/perception-gap.html
Kind: note

## The Perception Gap

I see it all the time in people close to me, on both sides of the aisle. The more news they consume, the more they paint the other side as a villain or a cartoon of evil.

There is a study behind the impression. In 2019 [More in Common](https://perceptiongap.us/) and YouGov asked 2,100 Americans what they believed and what they thought the other party believed. Democrats and Republicans imagined almost twice as many extremists among their opponents as there really are. The authors call the distance the perception gap.

The sharpest [finding](https://perceptiongap.us/) is about news. "The more news people consumed, the larger their Perception Gap." People who follow the news most of the time were nearly three times more distorted than those who follow it now and then. The authors are careful: "We can't prove that one causes the other." Sources on the right and on the left both came with larger gaps. Only the old broadcast networks came with smaller ones.

The effect is older than the internet. In the 1970s George Gerbner argued that heavy television viewers come to see the world as more dangerous than it is. He named it [mean world syndrome](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mean_world_syndrome). Swap danger for the other party and the machine is the same, now [tuned for engagement](monetization-model.md). [Steven Pinker](../mind/pinker.md) would have us [judge the world by data](https://news.harvard.edu/gazette/story/2019/06/focal-point-harvard-professor-steven-pinker-says-the-truth-lies-in-the-data/), not by anecdotes and images.

One friend and I butt heads over this, though we agree on most other things. He is firmly against Trump and still watches a lot of [Fox News](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Fox_News). He says he needs to see the world as its viewers see it, so that he can answer them. That is the strongest case for watching, and I take it seriously.

My reply is that this kind of news is not an honest picture of anyone, and the format is wrong for honest discussion. As far as I can tell it mostly leaves him angrier. One [experiment](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/30154168/) points the same way. People paid to follow the other side's voices on Twitter for a month did not move toward them. The Republicans among them moved further right.

It is the main reason I gave up most of the news I used to follow, [CNN](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/CNN) and Fox News among them. The study does not tell anyone what to watch. Cutting back was my own call.

==== Perception Management (Society) https://que.one/society/perception-management.html
Kind: take

## Perception Management

[Perception management](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Perception_management), as I see it, shapes public belief less through contact with reality than through stories that are chosen, framed, repeated, and amplified. Accuracy matters less than incentives, timing, emotional charge, and reach. It needs no central conspiracy. Institutions, platforms, and people repeating what feels useful produce it on their own.

Some campaigns are planned, like Russia's [troll farm](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Internet_Research_Agency) and [Cambridge Analytica](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Facebook%E2%80%93Cambridge_Analytica_data_scandal)'s work for the Trump campaign on Facebook data taken without consent. Britain's data regulator still found its methods [mostly ordinary](https://www.theregister.com/on-prem/2020/10/08/uk-privacy-watchdog-wraps-up-probe-into-cambridge-analytica-and-it-was-all-a-little-bit-overblown-no/411323). They ride the current more than they create it.

Stories are framed to benefit someone, and channels reward the vivid and simple. Repetition breeds familiarity mistaken for truth, the [illusory truth effect](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Illusory_truth_effect). Social pressure makes dissent costly, so weak claims outlive their merit. The [attention economy](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Attention_economy) rewards outrage, fear, and moral drama because [angry people click and share](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/34162706/). Each word about the political other side raises the odds of a share by 67 percent. The business side is the [monetization model](monetization-model.md).

Belief can drift far from reality without anyone consciously lying, because the system selects what travels, not what is accurate. My defenses: ask who benefits from the framing. Separate the event from its story. Watch for complex situations squeezed into moral theater. Distrust a claim pre-packaged for instant tribal reaction.

Perception management is the struggle to control the story people live inside. Ignore the incentives behind it and you will misread how mass belief forms. How truth can compete is under [viral truth](viral-truth.md).

==== Politics (Society) https://que.one/society/politics.html
Kind: take

## Politics

The classic poles of politics were named by [Thomas Sowell](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Thomas_Sowell) in [A Conflict of Visions](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/A_Conflict_of_Visions) as the constrained and unconstrained visions. [Steven Pinker](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Steven_Pinker) reworked them in [The Blank Slate](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Blank_Slate) as the tragic and utopian visions. They are the right and left we all argue about, and I am no exception.

I would rename the poles **Reason** and **Compassion**. Reason should guide us to a just and effective government. It should always be tempered by an understanding of human nature and by empathy in governing. The prudent stance is a hybrid, with the moment in history deciding what is practical.

[Sowell](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Thomas_Sowell)'s account seems largely right but partial to his libertarian reading of the constrained vision. I disagree that either vision is as likely to cause harm as the other. The harm each brings is particular to history, not to the vision. That opinion may be premature.

Many self-described centrists find conservatives hard to talk to because the conservative pole has moved to the right. The centrist position is reason plus compassion, leaning slightly left, and "balance" captures it.

Three smaller convictions. Vote for the politicians whose views and policies most closely match your own. The family and social class you are born into is sheer luck, the [lottery of birth](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lottery_of_birth), and it pays to remember it. And beware blinding, hateful feelings. Such feelings have fueled countless atrocities, and the dark side is more real than we think.

==== Rights and Remedies (Society) https://que.one/society/rights-remedies.html
Kind: take

## Rights and Remedies

A right you cannot enforce is not a right. The idea is as old as the republic. In [Marbury v. Madison](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Marbury_v._Madison), in 1803, Chief Justice John Marshall wrote that the United States would cease to be "a government of laws, and not of men." That would happen, he said, if its laws [furnish no remedy](https://www.law.cornell.edu/supremecourt/text/5/137) "for the violation of a vested legal right."

I think the Constitution is sound on paper. But paper is all it is until someone can walk into a court and get relief. The rights can stay in the text while the paths to enforce them narrow, and that is what I see happening.

Three paths have narrowed. [Qualified immunity](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Qualified_immunity) shields officials from damages unless the right they broke was "clearly established". In [2022](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Egbert_v._Boule) the Supreme Court declined to let citizens sue federal agents over new kinds of claims. In [2025](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Trump_v._CASA,_Inc.) it held that orders blocking a policy for everyone, not only for the people who sued, likely go beyond what courts may do.

Each ruling has its reasons, and judges should not make policy for the whole country from one courtroom. But the sum matters. A person wronged by the government now needs more money, more time, and a closer match to an old case than before.

So when I ask whether the [rule of law](rule-of-law.md) is holding, I no longer ask only what the text says. I ask who can still get a remedy, how fast, and at what cost.

==== Rule of Law (Society) https://que.one/society/rule-of-law.html
Kind: note

## Rule of Law

The [rule of law](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rule_of_law) means the law binds those who govern as much as the governed. In my reading the United States has lost ground on it, and the loss can be measured.

The [World Justice Project](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/World_Justice_Project) scores 143 countries each year. In its 2025 index the U.S. [ranks 27th](https://worldjusticeproject.org/rule-of-law-index/country/2025/United%20States). Its score fell for the third year running, on seven of eight measures, and the fall was the [sixth largest](https://businesslawtoday.org/2026/05/rule-of-law-recession-accelerates-authoritarian-trend-deepens-wjp-index-finds/) in the world. Two of those three years fell under Joe Biden, who [pardoned his own son](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hunter_Biden#Pardon_of_Hunter_Biden) after saying he would not. But since 2016 the U.S. score for limits on government power has dropped from 0.81 to 0.63.

Acts explain the numbers. On his first day back, [Donald Trump](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Donald_Trump) [pardoned](https://www.npr.org/2025/01/20/g-s1-36809/trump-pardons-january-6-riot) some 1,500 people charged over the [January 6 attack](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pardon_of_January_6_United_States_Capitol_attack_defendants), including rioters convicted of violence against police. Four days later he fired [17 inspectors general](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2025_dismissals_of_U.S._inspectors_general), the watchdogs inside federal agencies. A federal judge later found the firings [unlawful](https://federalnewsnetwork.com/agency-oversight/2025/09/trump-unlawfully-fired-17-agency-igs-judge-finds-but-wont-reinstate-them/).

He signed orders punishing law firms whose clients or causes he disliked, and [four judges out of four](https://www.npr.org/2025/06/27/g-s1-70443/trump-law-firm-susman-godfrey-ruling) struck them down as unconstitutional. His Justice Department indicted two of his adversaries, a former FBI director and New York's attorney general. A judge [threw out both cases](https://www.npr.org/2025/11/24/g-s1-98612/trump-us-attorney-lindsey-halligan) because the prosecutor had been unlawfully appointed.

His supporters have an answer. The [pardon power](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Federal_pardons_in_the_United_States) is the president's alone. Inspectors general serve at his pleasure. All true.

But the rule of law was never only about what is legal. It rests on [restraint](not-conservatism.md): powers held, and not used against enemies or for friends. When courts must say "unlawful" this often, restraint is what has gone.

[Pew](https://www.pewresearch.org/politics/2025/12/04/public-trust-in-government-1958-2025/) found 17% of Americans trusting Washington in September 2025, and the share has not passed 30% since 2007. But low trust is why this matters. A public that expects nothing from government will not [defend it](orban-playbook.md), and that suits [those who profit](oligarchy.md) from weak rules.

The courts held in every case above, and observers call the whole episode a [stress test](https://www.npr.org/2025/02/11/nx-s1-5293078/a-constitutional-stress-test-trump-executive-orders-are-challenged-in-court). By January 2026 one [tracker](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Legal_affairs_of_the_second_Trump_presidency#Tracking_the_cases) of [many](https://ucsd.libguides.com/usgov/trumptrackers) had counted 552 cases against the administration's actions, more than one a day. A stress test is meant to be run once, on purpose, by people who want the system to pass. No system is built to carry this load for years. The [checks among the branches](constitutional-republic.md) held. They are [worth defending](rights-remedies.md) before they are needed again.

==== Salomon's House (Society) https://que.one/society/salomons-house.html
Kind: note

## Salomon's House

Popular science would do better if its writers built on each other's work instead of starting over each time. Wikipedia already shows how. Its rule against [original research](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wikipedia:No_original_research) makes every article a synthesis of what others have published. I sometimes picture an order of science writers and explainers, held to a short charter:

1. No rule or act may undermine this charter or its mission.
2. Promote accurate knowledge and conduct by building and keeping beliefs and actions accurate and current.
3. Keep explanations logically consistent and as [simple](../mind/sense-of-style.md) as possible, so they are quick to absorb.
4. Respect the dignity and sovereignty of every participant, the audience included.

The idea is old. Francis Bacon imagined [Salomon's House](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/New_Atlantis), an order of sages whose work included telling nature from "impostures and illusions of all sorts."

Science itself is not loose. Peer review, journals, and societies make it the best-organized of the communities that keep our [trust in truth](../mind/trust-in-truth.md). What is loose is how it reaches the public, and that costs science respect. [Pew](https://www.pewresearch.org/science/2026/01/15/americans-confidence-in-scientists/) finds 77 percent of Americans have at least a fair amount of confidence in scientists, down from 87 percent in April 2020. In a [2024 survey](https://www.pewresearch.org/science/2024/11/14/public-trust-in-scientists-and-views-on-their-role-in-policymaking/), 47 percent said scientists "feel superior to others," and 45 percent called them good communicators. That is the [smug pilot](smug-pilots.md) problem, and rule 4 answers it.

Universities add a problem of their own. Jonathan Rauch warns of [two insurgencies](https://www.kirkusreviews.com/book-reviews/jonathan-rauch/the-constitution-of-knowledge/) against knowledge: troll culture, and "unforced conformity and ideological blacklisting, sometimes called cancel culture." On campuses, identity politics seems to feed the second. In [FIRE's 2025 survey](https://www.fire.org/news/2025-college-free-speech-rankings-expose-threats-first-amendment-rights-campus) of more than 58,000 students, 17 percent felt unable to voice an opinion for fear of the response. An order that argues about [claims, not persons](discourse.md), resists both.

The rules I write this site under are a one-person version of the same charter. Link to what someone already explained, source the claims, write plainly, and respect the reader.

==== Slow by Design (Society) https://que.one/society/slow-by-design.html
Kind: note

## Slow by Design

[Jonathan Haidt](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jonathan_Haidt) wrote in a [2022 essay](https://www.theatlantic.com/magazine/archive/2022/05/social-media-democracy-trust-babel/629369/) that the Framers "were excellent social psychologists." They knew a democracy rests on its people's judgment, and that judgment can run hot. A delegate's [notes](https://founders.archives.gov/documents/Madison/01-10-02-0044) record [James Madison](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/James_Madison) telling the Convention in 1787 that a people may want checks "against the turbulency and weakness of unruly passions." In [Federalist No. 10](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Federalist_No._10) he called the causes of faction "sown in the nature of man."

They built a republic that is slow on purpose. The design, Haidt writes, was to "slow things down, cool passions, require compromise." It also shielded leaders from "the mania of the moment" while voters judge them on Election Day. The features are under [Constitutional Republic](constitutional-republic.md).

Haidt's claim is that social media stripped the cooling away when platforms added the tools of virality, from 2009 to 2012. Anger moves faster than institutions can absorb it. The mechanics are under [Viral Truth](viral-truth.md), [The Perception Gap](perception-gap.md), and [Perception Management](perception-management.md). His warning: "If we do not make major changes soon, then our institutions, our political system, and our society may collapse."

I agree with Haidt, though the evidence is mixed and [we may both be wrong](../mind/popper.md).

A [2017 study](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/28928150/) found polarization grew most among the groups least likely to use social media, such as Americans over 65. Haidt's [reply](https://www.theatlantic.com/ideas/archive/2022/07/social-media-harm-facebook-meta-response/670975/) to a related study is that his claim concerns a sudden shift in the early 2010s, which decades-long trend lines cannot show.

The finding surprises me, and I have no full answer to it yet.

Haidt names three kinds of reform: harden democratic institutions, reform social media, and prepare the next generation. I back all three and would add two.

The first he practices without listing it. When people like him speak out calmly, with evidence, they build the critical mass that change needs. That is the [duty to speak](money-exception.md), with [civility](smug-pilots.md).

The second may be controversial. Slowness served the republic well. So far we have managed to "[keep it](https://en.wikiquote.org/wiki/Benjamin_Franklin)", in Franklin's phrase. But slowness cannot be the whole answer as technology speeds everything up.

I think AI can help us chill out. It could check facts at the speed of virality. It could tell me what Haidt, [Pinker](../mind/pinker.md), [Popper](../mind/popper.md), [Chomsky](../mind/chomsky.md), or [Rauch](../mind/trust-in-truth.md) would say about a thought of mine. Then I could admit sooner when I go astray. That depends on AI being [aligned](../tech/before-agi.md) with us, and earning our trust.

==== Smug Pilots (Society) https://que.one/society/smug-pilots.html
Kind: take

## Smug Pilots

In January 2017 The New Yorker ran a [cartoon](https://condenaststore.com/featured/these-smug-pilots-have-lost-touch-with-regular-will-mcphail.html) by [Will McPhail](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Will_McPhail). A passenger stands in the aisle of a plane and says: "These smug pilots have lost touch with regular passengers like us. Who thinks I should fly the plane?" All around him, hands go up.

I think media built for engagement helped put that passenger in the aisle. [Attention pays](monetization-model.md), and few things hold attention like someone taking on the experts. People learn to suspect and challenge specialists, which is healthy, and to do it in an improper way, which is not. Tom Nichols called the result [the death of expertise](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Death_of_Expertise).

The numbers are less dramatic but real. [Pew](https://www.pewresearch.org/science/2024/11/14/public-trust-in-scientists-and-views-on-their-role-in-policymaking/) found 87% of Americans confident in scientists in April 2020 and 76% in 2024.

Experts share the blame. When they bicker in public, ordinary people hear noise, not a debate. One [study](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/24117281/) found that people exposed to contradictory nutrition news grew more confused and came to doubt dietary advice in general.

Experts must disagree. That is how knowledge improves. But they ought to frame their disagreements with more civility, and say first what they agree on. Neil deGrasse Tyson's patient, line-by-line review of an amateur's physics, which I describe under [Dunning-Kruger](../mind/dunning-kruger.md), is the model. Respect for the listener is part of the expert's job.

==== Social Roles (Society) https://que.one/society/social-roles.html
Kind: reference

## Social Roles

A cheat-sheet of the roles people hold in society, kept for other entries to point to. In [role theory](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Role_theory), a role is the set of expectations a society attaches to a position, not a trait of the person. The theory maps the slots, not the people in them. What pulls a person toward a slot, and who ends up filling it, is partly evolved and partly temperament, as [Tooby](../mind/tooby.md) and [Domain-Specific Models](../mind/domain-specific-models.md) cover. Everyone holds several at once. The five domains below are my own grouping of the standard list, and the refinements are the field's own terms.

### Five domains

Each domain is defined by the institution that hands out the role and enforces it.

| Domain | Roles | How assigned | Who enforces |
|---|---|---|---|
| Kin | child, sibling, partner, parent, elder | at birth, later partly by choice | the family |
| Work | worker, provider, apprentice, colleague, boss, professional | by effort and choice | the employer and the trade |
| Civic | citizen, neighbor, taxpayer, voter, juror, soldier | by birthplace or residence | the state |
| Associational | friend, member, congregant, volunteer, fan, regular | by choice, and freely left | the group, through loyalty only |
| Transactional | customer, client, patient, student, guest, passenger | for the length of the exchange | the counterpart |

- A kin role can last a lifetime, and it is the first one anybody holds.
- A work role is the one that answers "what do you do?" in a market society.
- A civic role carries duties the state defines and can compel.
- An associational role carries the weakest sanctions, so it rests on loyalty.
- A transactional role is always paired with its complement: seller, provider, doctor, teacher, host, driver.

### Refinements

- **Ascribed versus achieved.** [Ralph Linton](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ralph_Linton) drew the line in 1936. An [ascribed](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ascribed_status) role comes from birth or circumstance: sex, age, kin, nationality. An [achieved](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Achieved_status) role comes from effort or choice: occupation, membership, parenthood. Most roles mix both over a life.
- **Roles come in pairs.** There is no parent without a child, no teacher without a student, no seller without a buyer. A role is a relationship, not a trait, though temperament steers who takes which role. That is the main difference from the mythic [archetypes](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jungian_archetypes): a Warrior stands alone, but a soldier needs a state.
- **Role set.** [Robert K. Merton](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Robert_K._Merton)'s term for the cluster of relationships one position carries. A teacher deals with students, parents, colleagues, administrators, and the school board, each with its own expectations.
- **Master status.** The one role that overrides the rest in how others see you, a term from Everett Hughes. Doctor, celebrity, convict, and disability all work as a [master status](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Master_status). Race and gender often act as one whether the person wants that or not.
- **Role conflict versus role strain.** [Conflict](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Role_conflict) is between two roles, such as parent and worker pulling in opposite directions. Strain is inside one role, such as a manager who must both support and evaluate the same person.
- **Life-course roles.** Child, student, worker, parent, retiree, elder. Societies mark each transition with a [rite of passage](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rite_of_passage). The transition is where the old script stops working and the new one is not yet learned.
- **Gender roles.** A cross-cutting ascribed layer that changes the expected script inside every other domain. Wikipedia covers the research under [gender role](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gender_role).
- **Front stage and back stage.** [Erving Goffman](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Erving_Goffman) described roles as [performances](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dramaturgy_(sociology)) for an audience, dropped in private. Role distance is the visible signal that someone is playing a role without owning it.
- **Deviant and marginal roles.** [Simmel's stranger](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Stranger_(sociology)) is near the group but not of it. [Talcott Parsons](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Talcott_Parsons)'s [sick role](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sick_role) excuses the sick person from normal duties and obliges them to seek help and try to recover. [Labeling theory](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Labeling_theory) adds that being called deviant is itself a role assignment, and one that tends to stick.

### Mythic roles versus social roles

The Sage, the Warrior, and the Peacemaker of myth map onto social roles, but loosely. The Sage is the teacher or expert, a work role. The Warrior is the soldier or police officer, a civic role. Peacemaking is usually a function inside another role rather than a role of its own: elders, parents, judges, and diplomats all do it. The standalone version appears only when a society formalizes it, as [mediator](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mediation) or [ombudsman](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ombudsman). The oldest mythic set, sovereign and priest, warrior, and producer, is the [trifunctional](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Trifunctional_hypothesis) division Georges Dumézil found across Indo-European societies.

A role is held, not owned. [Reflexivity](../mind/reflexivity.md) is the ability to see and change one's own roles, and [Hold Your Identity Lightly](../mind/identity-lightly.md) makes the same case for labels.

==== Trans Issues (Society) https://que.one/society/trans-issues.html
Kind: take

## Trans Issues

On trans issues I reject two things: the moral panic on the right and the censorious absolutism on the left.

The panic is out of scale. In December 2024, NCAA president Charlie Baker told senators he knew of [fewer than 10](https://www.npr.org/2024/12/17/nx-s1-5231991/ncaa-charlie-baker-sports-gambling-regulations-senate) transgender athletes among more than half a million. In 2022 Utah's Republican governor, [Spencer Cox](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Spencer_Cox), counted 4 among 75,000 high school athletes, one of them in girls' sports. "Rarely has so much [fear and anger](https://www.nbcnews.com/nbc-out/out-news/utah-governor-becomes-latest-republican-veto-transgender-sports-ban-rcna21116) been directed at so few," he wrote. Bans and demonization answer a threat the numbers do not show. They are illiberal backlash, not serious policy.

The absolutism is real too. Open scientific talk about sex differences, and good-faith disagreement over language or policy, are not violence. Treating them as violence corrodes liberal norms. In youth medicine, prudence matters: England's [Cass Review](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cass_Review) found the evidence for puberty blockers and hormones in young people weak. Rigor is not prohibition, and questioning evidence is not bigotry.

Culture wars like this one are what free societies go through as people claim equal rights. What I support is equal civil rights, protection from harassment, and basic dignity, with no metaphysical dogma in either direction. When politics becomes exaggerated threats, zero-sum thinking, and silenced dissent, it signals a [moral panic](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Moral_panic). The antidote is free inquiry, evidence, and durable institutions, not strongmen, purges, or enforced consensus.

==== The Two-Front War (Society) https://que.one/society/two-front-war.html
Kind: note

## The Two-Front War

A serious illness in America means a war on two fronts. One is the disease. The other is the bill. The first is nature's doing. The second is ours, and it is the one we could end.

The numbers show the second front. The U.S. spent [17.2 percent of its economy](https://www.healthsystemtracker.org/chart-collection/health-spending-u-s-compare-countries/) on health in 2024, against 11.2 percent in comparable wealthy countries. Per person that was $14,775, nearly twice their average. What it buys is [a shorter life](https://www.healthsystemtracker.org/chart-collection/u-s-life-expectancy-compare-countries/): 79.0 years at birth, 3.7 below the peer average. Brand-name drugs cost [4.2 times](https://www.healthday.com/health-news/general-health/us-prescription-drug-prices-nearly-triple-those-of-other-nations) what they cost in 33 other countries, though generics are cheaper here.

The patient pays for the gap. [KFF estimates](https://www.kff.org/health-costs/the-burden-of-medical-debt-in-the-united-states/) that about 14 million adults owe more than $1,000 in medical debt, and 3 million owe more than $10,000. Together Americans owe at least $220 billion. [Hundreds of hospitals](https://kffhealthnews.org/health-care-costs/medical-debt-hospitals-sue-patients-threaten-credit-khn-investigation/) sue patients or threaten their credit. They include for-profit chains, nonprofit Catholic systems, and public university hospitals, so the problem is not one kind of owner.

Barbara and John Ehrenreich named the [medical-industrial complex](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Medical%E2%80%93industrial_complex) in 1969, after [Eisenhower's](money-exception.md) warning about its military cousin. In 1980 [Arnold Relman](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/7412851/), then editor of the New England Journal of Medicine, warned of care run as a business. Care is one of the goods that [distorts when treated as a product](markets-capitalism.md). The buyer is sick, scared, and in no position to shop. The market's usual discipline, walking away when the price is wrong, is the one thing a patient cannot do.

So the second front is a choice of rules, not a law of nature. Other rich countries spend about half as much per person and live longer, under many different systems. The [2025 Medicaid cuts](oligarchy.md) moved the other way. A sick person should only have to fight the disease.

==== U.S. Identity Politics (Society) https://que.one/society/us-identity-politics.html
Kind: take

## U.S. Identity Politics

[Identity politics](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Identity_politics) is not a recent infection, as I read it. Identity has always organized the U.S. party system. What changed is visibility and [polarization](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Political_polarization_in_the_United_States).

The Democratic coalition gathers minority status, city life, higher education, and cosmopolitan values, held together by a shared self-image of inclusion. The Republican coalition gathers cultural continuity, national belonging, religion, and a felt loss of status. Its markers are appeals to "real Americans" and "traditional values." Partisan sorting has squeezed many identities into one label, so [disagreement lands as personal offense](trans-issues.md). Social media pours gasoline on this by rewarding outrage and certainty and punishing nuance. The mechanism is in the [monetization model](monetization-model.md).

U.S. politics is identity-first, with policy reasoned out afterward. Parties sell moral stories to different kinds of people. Voters buy the one that flatters their self-image and their fears. Once identity is engaged, reason becomes a lawyer, not a judge.

My impression of [Donald Trump](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Donald_Trump)'s supporters, not survey data, is that they want rid of what they see harming the country. They fear [immigration](immigration-choice.md) and the loss of their rights, and they see the opposition as entirely corrupt. That caricature has consequences.

The exit is a centrist coalition that rejects tribal loyalty as a virtue. It borrows working ideas from both sides and treats disagreement as information rather than heresy. As an individual, opt out. Refuse to [signal](virtue-signaling.md), caricature, or dehumanize, since every act of performative outrage feeds a machine that is paid to keep the temperature up.

==== Viral Truth (Society) https://que.one/society/viral-truth.html
Kind: take

## Viral Truth

[Misinformation](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Misinformation) spreads faster than truth. Lies are simpler, more emotional, and cheaper to produce. The [attention economy](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Attention_economy) is tuned for exactly those traits, and [trust in experts](smug-pilots.md) pays part of the bill. Truth does not spread by default. If it is to compete, I think it has to be built for the same terrain.

Five principles truth-tellers can borrow from the way lies travel, without borrowing their ethics:

| # | Principle | Action |
|---|-----------|--------|
| 1 | Speed | [Pre-bunk](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Prebunking) predictable falsehoods; prepare quick summaries in advance; verify fast, not perfectly. |
| 2 | Simplicity | One idea per message, one sentence that survives a screenshot, one visual when possible. |
| 3 | Trusted messengers | Insiders, local voices, and former skeptics persuade; [village tours](https://www.wilsoncenter.org/article/hungarys-turning-point) helped [unseat Orbán](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2026_Hungarian_parliamentary_election). |
| 4 | Repetition | Repetition builds memory and silence leaves room for lies; repeating truth is not propaganda. Silence also feeds [pluralistic ignorance](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pluralistic_ignorance): each person privately doubts, yet assumes everyone else believes. |
| 5 | Asymmetry | Focus on the persuadable middle, strengthen allies who amplify, accept that not everyone can be reached. |

What truth must not borrow is the rest of the playbook: manufactured anger, [dehumanizing people](perception-gap.md), and social punishment for dissent. Those are the mechanics [perception management](perception-management.md) describes and the [Discourse Protocol](discourse.md) exists to refuse. Using them for a good cause still trains the audience to respond to outrage rather than evidence. Truth borrows distribution, not cruelty.

==== Virtue Signaling (Society) https://que.one/society/virtue-signaling.html
Kind: note

## Virtue Signaling

[Virtue signaling](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Virtue_signalling) is a form of hypocrisy: projecting moral values for social approval while avoiding real-world action. A post, a slogan, or a symbol costs little. Doing something about the cause costs time, money, or standing.

My twist is that it is often unintentional. Good intentions get mixed with hidden self-interest, or with a little subconscious narcissism, and the person doing it rarely notices. That is why it is so common. Most of us would rather feel good about a stance than pay for it.

The charge itself deserves care. [Critics of the term](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Virtue_signalling) point out that accusing someone of virtue signaling can be its own kind of signaling. Research also finds that people accused of it often feel genuine outrage. Calling a view virtue signaling dismisses the speaker without answering the view, the mistake known as [Bulverism](../mind/famous-lessons.md#bulverism).

So I use one test, on others and on myself: what did the stance cost? A moral view that comes with action, money, or risk is not signaling, whatever its tone. One that comes with none may be sincere, but it has not yet done anything.

==== Who Opened the Door (Society) https://que.one/society/who-opened-the-door.html
Kind: take

## Who Opened the Door

I am Dominican-American, and I see a missed opportunity among dark-skinned Latinos, Dominicans included. Black Americans opened a door that we walked through, and too many of us forget it.

The case against my view deserves its due. Latin America has long treated race as a blend, called [mestizaje](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mestizo#Mestizaje_in_Latin_America), rather than as fixed boxes. Latinos also fought their own civil-rights battles, such as [Mendez v. Westminster](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mendez_v._Westminster). So it is no surprise that when [Pew](https://www.pewresearch.org/short-reads/2022/05/02/about-6-million-u-s-adults-identify-as-afro-latino/) asked Afro-Latino adults their race, only a quarter said Black.

Still, the door was opened by Black Americans. The [Voting Rights Act](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Voting_Rights_Act_of_1965) of 1965 was won mainly by and for them. Its [1975 extension](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Voting_Rights_Act_of_1965#Amendments) reached "language minorities", people of Spanish heritage among them, and required bilingual ballots where they were numerous. [Barbara Jordan](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Barbara_Jordan), a Black congresswoman from Houston, backed the extension, and it covered Hispanics in Texas.

I see the debt go unpaid in two ways. Among Dominicans, it is [anti-Haitian](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Anti-Haitian_sentiment_in_the_Dominican_Republic) attitudes toward our neighbors on the same island. A court ruling there left hundreds of thousands of Dominicans of Haitian descent stateless. Here, it is voting for politicians who would roll back the civil-rights protections that cover Latinos too.

I am not asking anyone to check a new box. [Hold the label lightly](../mind/identity-lightly.md) and the debt firmly. That means solidarity with Black Americans, a more open mind about the border back home, remembering who opened the door, and voting accordingly.

==== Who We Thank (Society) https://que.one/society/who-we-thank.html
Kind: take

## Who We Thank

I served in the military, so I know how hard people in uniform work and how proud they are. They take risks few civilian jobs carry, so the honor they get at ballparks is not misplaced. But it is excessive and selective.

It is excessive because other professions that serve get so little of it. Each [Major League Baseball](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Major_League_Baseball) team plays 81 home games. I would give at least half of those to honoring doctors, nurses, teachers, firefighters, police, and clergy. They work tireless hours for the rest of us and rarely get the same honor.

It is selective because easy reverence skips how troops are used. [James Fallows](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/James_Fallows) made that case in "The Tragedy of the American Military": a public that reveres the troops pays little attention to their wars. Some of the cheering was even bought. From 2012 to 2015 the Pentagon [paid](https://www.stripes.com/news/dozens-of-pro-sports-teams-involved-in-paid-patriotism-1.376973) dozens of pro teams, ten in baseball, for those tributes.

My criticism starts with the [military-industrial complex](money-exception.md) and with [Smedley Butler](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/War_Is_a_Racket), a Marine general who called war a racket. The military is not misused all the time. But since 2001, too many operations seem aimed at foreign affairs with little bearing on everyday Americans, especially the working-class fan watching the game.

Veterans also get forgotten, most of all their health. It took a comedian, [Jon Stewart](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jon_Stewart), to help pass the [PACT Act](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Honoring_our_PACT_Act_of_2022) for veterans sickened by [burn pits](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Burn_pit). As far as I can find, no ballpark has honored him. One should.

==== Whose Problem (Society) https://que.one/society/whose-problem.html
Kind: note

## Whose Problem

I keep asking which problems a billionaire should obsess over. Two answered with their own money. [Yvon Chouinard](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Yvon_Chouinard) gave Patagonia to a trust and a nonprofit so its profits fight climate change. [Bill Gates](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gates_Foundation) funds the fight against outbreaks and, through [TerraPower](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/TerraPower), safer nuclear power, which also fights climate change. Both picked foundational problems, whose solutions solve other problems.

The first test is whether the problem is real. [Sabine Hossenfelder](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sabine_Hossenfelder) argues some famous problems in physics are not problems, only discomfort with how the numbers look. A real problem is a clash between theory and observation.

The [Department of Government Efficiency](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Department_of_Government_Efficiency) defined the problem as bloat. Analysts at [Brookings](https://www.brookings.edu/articles/cut-the-government-with-a-scalpel-not-an-axe) and the [Manhattan Institute](https://www.concordcoalition.org/facing-the-future/the-2025-agenda-debt-and-taxes/) said at the start that the money was not there: most spending is benefits, defense, and interest. The promised two trillion dollars shrank to [a disputed fraction](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Department_of_Government_Efficiency). Then [Elon Musk](https://www.aljazeera.com/news/2025/6/3/elon-musk-slams-trumps-signature-budget-bill-as-a-disgusting-abomination) called the 2025 spending law "a disgusting abomination" for raising the deficit. His own objection conceded that deficits are written by law, not by bloat. The toxicity of X, formerly Twitter, is by contrast a real problem, the kind [Haidt warns about](slow-by-design.md).

The second test is who should own it. Frame a problem as one person's, and the fix lives and dies with them. That is three risks in one: control, [ego](../life/legacy.md), and continuity. Frame it as a public problem and we all own it, under rules that outlast any donor. The [money sits on both sides](oligarchy.md) of politics. So the question is not whether the rich are good, but whether one basket should hold all the eggs.

Open source shows the answer's shape. Much of the internet runs on code kept by unpaid volunteers. That is how a burned-out maintainer handed the keys to a stranger, who slipped [a backdoor](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/XZ_Utils_backdoor) into a library on most Linux systems.

The fixes that work are collective. Germany's [Sovereign Tech Agency](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sovereign_Tech_Fund) pays maintainers with public money. [Alpha-Omega](https://alpha-omega.dev/) pools money from big technology firms for security work. Neither depends on one patron.

I once thought the tension was [fast against slow](../mind/two-systems.md), individual against group. It is not. A billionaire can think slowly, and a committee can panic. The real tension is ownership, ego, and continuity, and rules fix those, not a better billionaire.

So yes, obsess, and give. [Forbes](https://www.globalcitizen.org/en/content/forbes-400-philanthropy-score/) grades the giving. Someone should grade what it fixed. Then hand the problem back to the rest of us.

==== AI (Tech) https://que.one/tech/ai.html
Kind: note

## AI

Notes I keep on working with AI models. How I see the software worth building before AGI is on its own page ([Software Before AGI](before-agi.md)). Everything here has a sell-by date, because what models can do has been changing faster than these notes.

### Prompts that keep answers honest

Two prompts I reuse whenever being right matters more than being fast:

- `Do a thorough review of X, then adversarially double-check your conclusion for accuracy.`
- `Assess the claim and provide a concise take.`

### Run DeepSeek Locally

Use [ollama](https://github.com/ollama/ollama) for this.

Pick the DeepSeek R1 model you want to try: 7b (4.7GB) - 14b (9G) - 32b (20GB) - 70b (43GB) - 671b (404GB)

```bash
brew install ollama                   # Install ollama
ollama serve                          # Start ollama - in a diff shell window
ollama pull deepseek-r1:7b            # Pull deepseek-r1:7b
ollama run deepseek-r1:7b             # Run it
alias r1='ollama run deepseek-r1:7b'  # Setup a shell alias to prompt question
```

### Embeddings

[Embeddings](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Word_embedding) are lists of numbers that stand for data and capture its meaning or its relations. For example, `"cat" → [0.12, -0.83, 0.45, ...]`, a list of a few hundred to a few thousand numbers. They are widely used for finding similar items, ranking, and grouping.

#### Common Patterns

The most common use is semantic search. Embed a set of documents and a query, then find the nearest neighbors (FAISS, Annoy, ScaNN, Pinecone). No text-generating model is needed.

Recommendation engines use the same idea. They place users and items in one shared space and rank by distance (Spotify, YouTube, Amazon). Fraud and anomaly detection embed transactions or log lines and flag the outliers. Clustering and deduplication group similar items for topic discovery, customer segments, or duplicate detection.

Code search maps plain-language queries and code into the same space (Sourcegraph's older approach, GitHub code search before Copilot). Finally, classification embeds inputs and compares them against class centers or a simple linear layer. That is faster and cheaper than calling a full LLM (for example Sentence-BERT for duplicate-question detection or support-ticket routing).

#### When Embeddings Are Enough

For tasks about matching, ranking, or grouping, embeddings alone are often enough. They are faster, cheaper, more predictable, and easier to debug than reaching for an LLM.

Current as of September 2026.

==== Arcade (Tech) https://que.one/tech/arcade.html
Kind: reference

## Arcade
Bits on playing the old-style coin-operated video arcade games. You can buy the actual old game cabinets from eBay and other places. Or you can set up [MAME](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/MAME) on your desktop, using game ROMs you legally own. Or you can build you own game cabinet, with a small dedicated computer running running MAME.

### MAME on Your Desktop
MAME originally stood for Multiple Arcade Machine Emulator, but nowadays it means much more than that. As its website states: 

    MAME is a hardware emulator: it faithfully reproduces the behavior of many
    arcade machines (it is not a simulation). This program is not a game but can
    directly, through ROM images, run the complete system of these old arcade
    machines. These ROMs are subject to copyright and it is in most of the cases
    illegal to use them if you do not own the arcade machine.

To set up MAME, do the following:
- Install the latest MAME binary using your OS package installer. On macOS you can just do `brew install mame`
- Copy the ROM zip files into the `~/.mame/roms/` directory
- Run any specific game from the CLI with `mame stargate`
- Install [`manu`](https://github.com/queone/manu), a small Go util that reads above roms directory and prompts for what game to run 

Read more in the [MAME Reference](https://docs.mamedev.org/index.html).

### MAME on Raspberry Pi

- Install Ubuntu 24.04 desktop on Raspberry Pi 5
- This assumes you're using Apple **macOS** to do all this
- Use an SD card of at least 16GB in size
- Insert the SD card on your Mac
- `brew install raspberry-pi-imager`
- Run the Imager and burn the latest Ubuntu Desktop image
- Once done, insert the SD card on your Pi5 and install Ubuntu
  
#### Ideal Arcade Monitor
The ideal arcade computer monitor is the **ViewSonic** 4/3 aspect ratio **VG939Sm** monitor. The Model No = VS15843.

#### Additional configurations and settings follow below

Below are some general guidelines and configuration settings for such a setup, but you'll need to improvise where necessary.

##### Adjust CLI Console Character size

```bash
sudo mount -o remount,rw /boot/firmware
sudo vi /boot/firmware/cmdline.txt
Remove the 'quiet splash' at the end, and add 'video=800x600' or 1024x768 ; 1280x720 ; 1920x1080
sudo vi /boot/firmware/config.txt
Add below
hdmi_group=2
hdmi_mode=16  # 9=800x600 ; 16=1024x768 ; 4=1280x720 ; 82=1920x1080
dtparam=pciex1_gen=2
```

If necessary, you can make further adjustments via `dpkg-reconfigure` utility: 

```bash
sudo apt install console-setup kbd   # To optionally install addtional Font Sizes
sudo dpkg-reconfigure console-setup
Select Terminus                      # Default is VGA
Select Font Size 8x14, or whatever
```

##### Setup SSH

```bash
sudo systemctl enable ssh
sudo systemctl start ssh
```

##### Disable desktop

```bash
sudo systemctl set-default multi-user.target
sudo reboot
sudo systemctl start graphical.target        # To manually start the Graphical Desktop
sudo systemctl set-default graphical.target  # To re-enable Graphical Desktop
```

##### Auto-login setup

To set default user for automatic login, edit the getty service: 

```bash
sudo mkdir -p /etc/systemd/system/getty@tty1.service.d/
sudo vi /etc/systemd/system/getty@tty1.service.d/override.conf

Add below:

[Service]
ExecStart=
ExecStart=-/sbin/agetty --autologin USERNAME --noclear %I $TERM

# Note: Replace USERNAME with the actual username

sudo systemctl daemon-reload
sudo systemctl restart getty@tty1.service
sudo reboot
```

##### Issues
- If the keyboard does not respond when the **manu** menu comes up, check the user's permissions. Add the user to the input group with `sudo usermod -a -G input $USER`.

#### Set New Hostname

```bash
sudo hostnamectl set-hostname <NEW-HOSTNAME>
sudo vi /etc/hosts  # Change it here too
sudo reboot
```

#### Ensure Sound is Working

Plug a USB-to-3.5mm audio connector to the Raspberry Pi 5 and connect that to your speakers. Test with below steps: 

```bash
sudo apt update
sudo apt install --reinstall pipewire pipewire-pulse wireplumber pipewire-audio-client-libraries
sudo apt install --reinstall libspa-0.2-bluetooth
pactl info | grep "Server Name"
pactl list short sinks
aplay /usr/share/sounds/alsa/Front_Center.wav  # To test speaker
```

#### Install MAME

To download and install the latest MAME binary. Use the binaries located at <https://stickfreaks.com/>. Note that they use **7 Zip** for compression. Note also, that this setup puts certain binaries under the `$HOME/bin/` directory.

```bash
cd ~/bin
curl -LO https://stickfreaks.com/mame/mame_0.281_debian_13_trixie_arm64.7z
sudo apt install 7zip
7z x mame_0.281_debian_13_trixie_arm64.7z -omame_0.281
ln -sf mame_0.281/mame mame
```

So the **mame** binary will reside at `$HOME/bin/mame`, and remember that the standard MAME configurations normally reside under the `$HOME/.mame` directory.

#### Compile MAME?

If you decide to compile MAME yourself, which allows you to select only the machines you are interested in, follow below instructions.

##### Install required packages and clone MAME repo 

```bash
sudo apt update
sudo apt install build-essential libsdl2-dev libfontconfig1-dev libpulse-dev \
  qtbase5-dev qtchooser qt5-qmake qtbase5-dev-tools libqt5opengl5-dev \
  libasound2-dev libxinerama-dev libxi-dev libgl1-mesa-dev python3
sudo apt install libsdl2-ttf-dev

git clone https://github.com/mamedev/mame.git
cd mame
```

##### Initial Compilation

You will need to do a **full compilation** first, in roder to build the needed `emu.h` and other core headers. This ***can take a long time**: 

```bash
time make clean
rm -rf obj
time make SUBTARGET=mame SOURCES="src/mame/skeleton/testpat.cpp" REGENIE=1 NOWERROR=1 -j$(nproc)
```

Note that `emu.h` and the `.pch` files aren’t part of the source tree, and they are ONLY generated during a **full regular build**. This pre-step is a requirement in order to later do a restricted SOURCES build of a "tiny" MAME binary with only selected games.

##### Prepare Source Files

From the root of the checked out `mame` directory: 

```bash
$ cat src/mame/custom/custom.mak
# Custom build for specific games

SOURCES += src/mame/capcom/1942.cpp
SOURCES += src/mame/namco/galaga.cpp
SOURCES += src/mame/pacman/pacman.cpp
SOURCES += src/mame/midway/williams.cpp

$ cat src/mame/custom.lst
@source:capcom/1942.cpp
1942            // (c) Capcom

@source:namco/galaga.cpp
galaga          // (c) Namco
galagamf        // (c) Namco
galagamk        // (c) Namco

@source:pacman/pacman.cpp
mspacman        // (c) Namco/Midway

@source:midway/williams.cpp
stargate        // (c) Williams
```

##### Tiny Compilation

```bash
time make SUBTARGET=mame SOURCES="src/mame/capcom/1942.cpp,src/mame/namco/galaga.cpp,src/mame/pacman/pacman.cpp,src/mame/midway/williams.cpp" REGENIE=1 NOWERROR=1 OPTIMIZE=3 USE_QTDEBUG=1 -j$(nproc)

# Confirm version and list of supported games
./mame -version
./mame -listfull
```

#### Boot into manu Binary

Boot into default `manu` Game Menu binary - See <https://github.com/queone/manu>

You may also want to update your `$HOME/.bashrc` file with below snippet, so that this special menu utility always run: 

```bash
# Always run manu menu binary. See https://github.com/queone/manu
while true; do
    manu
done
```

#### Configure MAME USB Controller

Before configuring MAME, make sure the OS is able to read the joystick controller and buttons:

```bash
sudo apt-get install joystick
jstest /dev/input/js0
# Then press the buttons and joystick controls to confirm
```

Once the OS can read the controller, configure it **within** MAME itself. Press **TAB** on an attached keyboard, and MAME lets you configure the buttons. For more info see the [MAME documentation pages](https://docs.mamedev.org/index.html).


### Creating USB Installers

- Download the desired ISO using `curl -LO` (see below).
- You will need an empty USB drive of 16GB or more in size.
- Create the USB using below instructions, which are for macOS, and therefore require the ISO be converted to DMG format: 

```bash
curl -LO https://github.com/substring/os/releases/download/2023.11/groovyarcade-2023.11-x86_64.iso.xz
xz -d groovyarcade-2023.11-x86_64.iso.xz
hdiutil convert groovyarcade-2023.11-x86_64.iso -format UDRW -o groovyarcade-2023.11-x86_64
diskutil list 
diskutil unmountDisk /dev/disk4
sudo dd status=progress bs=1m if=groovyarcade-2023.11-x86_64.dmg of=/dev/rdisk4
diskutil unmountDisk /dev/disk4
```

Now remove USB from your Mac, and in short, you'll need to:

- Ensure that the target system allows booting off of a USB drive
- Insert USB into target system and follow the OS installation instructions

==== Azure Data Factory (ADF) (Tech) https://que.one/tech/azure/adf/
Kind: reference

## Azure Data Factory (ADF)

- Definition: A cloud-based data integration service THAT 
    orchestrates data movement and transformation BETWEEN
    direct data sources <and> compute resources
- How it works:
    Connect and collect
    Transform and enrich 
    CI/CD publish
    Monitor and alerts
- Most common "data integration pattern" = ETL (Extract/Transform/Load)
  - ADF has code-free ETL as a service
  - Option to do hard-coded transformation using Azure compute
  - Mapping data flow provide a UI-wizard to simplify your pipeline setup (5 aspects)
      1. Ingest data 
      2. Control flow
      3. Data flow
      4. Schedule ops
      5. Monitor ops  
- Components:
    Pipelines
    Activities
    Datasets
    Linked Services
    Dataflows
    Integration Runtimes
- Key terms:
    Control flow
    Pipeline run
    Triggers
    Parameters
    Variables
- PIPELINES: A logical grouping of ACTIVITIES that perform one unit of work 
  - ADF can have one of more pipelines
- ACTIVITIES: Represent a single "processing step" in the pipeline
  - Three (3) types of activities supported by ADF:
    - Data movement
    - Data transformation
    - Control
- DATASETS: Represent data structure giving selected view into data store
  - Points to the specific data SUBSET to use in activity
  - For input and output
- LINKED SERVICES (?)
- Mapping DATAFLOWS: 
  - Two (2) uses:
    - Represent data source (for INGEST)
    - Represent compute resource (for TRANSFORM)
  - Represent connection information to link ADF to external services
  - Works closely with datasets: This specifies HOW to connedt & datasets defines WHAT data looks like
- INTEGRATION RUNTIMES (IR):
  - Compute infrastructure used by ADF to provide FULLY MANAGED:
      1. Dataflows
      2. Data movements
      3. Activity dispatch
      4. SSIS Package Execution
  - Automatically manages Spart clusters
  - Three (3) IR types:
      1. Azure SSIS (SQL Server Integration Services) package execution (public or private)
      2. Self hosted; Activity dispatch & Data movements (public or private)
      3. Azure; Activity dispatch & Data movements & Dataflows (public or private)
  - Hybrid solution, depending on your networking needs

- Microsoft diagram:  <https://docs.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/data-factory/media/introduction/data-factory-visual-guide.png>

==== Azure (Tech) https://que.one/tech/azure/
Kind: reference

## Azure 
Helpful Microsoft Azure cloud bits.

- [Github Workflow OIDC Access to Azure](../git/oidc-azure.md)
- [Understanding Microsoft Access Token Validation](ms-token-validation.md): Why only the intended resource should validate an access token, and the Azure Management exception.

### Azure Cloud

The __cloud__ metaphor usually evokes a feeling of something that is experienced without understanding what it is or how it works, and Microsoft Azure [cloud computing](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cloud_computing) if no different.

To avoid the hype, let's approach the Azure Cloud as revolving around two major realms: **Resource** and **Security**. This is not how Microsoft typically documents Azure, but it's a more helpful perspective on how it is put together and how it works. In essence, the Azure cloud can be summarized by its two fundamental realms: Azure Resource Services and Azure Security Services.

### Azure Resource Services

What we call _Azure **Resource** Services_ here is essentially the comprehensive suite of [Products](https://azure.microsoft.com/en-us/products/) and tools to host applications, store data, and enable various services on Microsoft's Azure cloud. Institutions can access these wide array of **Azure Services** which include virtual machines (VM), databases, storage solutions, machine learning, artificial intelligence (AI), serverless computing, content delivery networks (CDN), and much more. The functions of these services are primarily managed via the Azure Resource Manager API at <https://management.azure.com>, and are detailed at <https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/azure-resource-manager>. Azure services are the core of the Azure ecosystem.

See below pages for specific bits on specific services:

- [Azure Data Factory (ADF)](adf/index.md): A cloud-based data integration service that orchestrates data movement and transformation between direct data compute resources.

### Azure Security Services

What we call _Azure **Security** Services_ here is essentially what Microsoft calls its _[Microsoft Identity Platform](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/entra/identity-platform/)_, and it plays a fundamental role in the Azure ecosystem, that permeates all of Azure. Like Azure Resources, it is a complementary suite of services that provides several essential cloud identity components, allowing institutions to control and manage access to services and applications that they host on Azure.

- [Microsoft Entra ID](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/entra/fundamentals/what-is-entra) (formerly known as Azure Active Directory): This is the key element that serves as the primary **identity provider** for Azure, with tools and services to control and protect access to azure services and applications. It plays a vital role within the overall Azure identity and access management ([IAM](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/entra/fundamentals/identity-fundamental-concepts)) framework for any institution. At a very high level, IAM can be summarized as the core framework that enables an organization to facilitate **1)** the right individuals, **2)** to access the right resources, **3)** at the right time, and **4)** for the right reasons. The Microsoft Entra ID functions are managed via the [MS Graph](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/graph/overview) API, typically via the <https://graph.microsoft.com> endpoint.
- Other important Azure security services are [Azure Policy](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/governance/policy/overview) and [Microsoft Entra Privileged Identity Management (PIM)](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/entra/id-governance/privileged-identity-management/pim-configure). Moreover, the [Azure Security](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/security/fundamentals/overview) page lists other essential elements within Azure security services.

### Azure Management Hierarchy

To manage access into Azure resource or security services you must first understand that these are indeed two (2) separate _realms_, but they are very closely _intertwined_. The Resource Realm is where Azure service objects live, and the Security Realm is where, well, security objects live. Luckily, these realms share the same hierarchy, which starts at the top, within an organization's Azure **tenant**.

- Tenant: This is the top of the hierarchy. It is here where all **security** objects such as Users, Groups, and Roles reside (for a list of all object types see _Services and features_ in the [Overview of Microsoft Graph](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/graph/overview)).
- Tenant Root Group: A special top-level object, essentially the same as the Tenant itself, but where all **resource** objects live. It is of resource type _Management Group_ (MG). This root MG can have other sub MGs defined underneath it, as well as individual subscriptions.
- Management Group (MG): This is where Azure subscriptions live. It is an object that allows an organization to logically arrange its resources.
- Subscription: This is where resource groups live. It is an additional _bucket_ that an organization can use to logically organize its resources.
- Resource Group (RG): This is where individual resources live. It is yet another _sub bucket_ to logically organized resources with the hierarchy.
- Individual Resource: This is an actual service object, such a VM, or a storage account. For more info on resource types see [What is Azure Resource Manager](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/azure-resource-manager/management/overview) and [Azure products](https://azure.microsoft.com/en-us/products/).

> **Note**<br>
[Stack Overflow has this really good entry](https://stackoverflow.com/questions/47307368/what-is-the-difference-between-an-azure-tenant-and-azure-subscription), highlighting the relation of these objects within an Azure tenant.

**Important:**<br>
1. All security objects are available cross the entire individual tenant's hierarchy.
2. Organizations typically have multiple tenants, such as a **Development** tenant for a testing environment, and a **Production** one for their live environment, and so on.
3. Security objects are typically __not__ shared cross tenants, except for special objects that do support a more advanced and rare multi-tenant configuration.
4. Resource objects that are defined or deployed to only one area of the hierachy, are only available within that area. For instance, if a resource Role Based Access Control (RBAC) role _definition_ is deployed only to subscription A, it cannot be _assigned/consumed_ within subscription B.
5. It is almost always better to define resource objects, such as resource RBAC role definitions, at the _very top of the hierarchy_, the Tenant Root Group. That way they are always available to be used anywhere within the entire tenant.
6. Microsoft Azure makes available native, **Built-In** Entra ID roles (security realm) as well as resource RBAC roles (resource realm) for each service product offering. Microsoft makes these roles available globally, to every organization with a tenant in Azure cloud.
7. Many organization choose to create their own **Custom** roles based on the Built-In ones, because it affords them better version control of these roles. Microsoft is known for changing Built-In role behavior from time to time, and having your own _pinned_version of a role offers more control.

### Azure Access Methods

To do work in azure, whether to create resource or security objects, or to manage them, you have to access Azure in one of the following ways:

| Method | Secret | Typical Use |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Azure CLI | Yes, secured via browser popup | Interactive command line |
| OIDC | No | CI/CD automation |
| SP | Yes | Services and Application automated access |
| MI | No | Services and Application automated access |

Typical use column only describes the most common reason for using the specific method, but actual usage can vary depending on context.

### Create VM

Create a sample Azure VM using the `az` utility.

- Create VM, resource, group and VNET all at once
```bash
az vm create --name myvm01 --resource-group myrs --admin-username admin --admin-password secure --image "OpenLogic:CentoOS:7.6:7.6.20190402" --vnet name myvnet --subnet mysubnet --size Standard_B1ms
```

- Create VM into existing subnet (need subnet ID)
```bash
az vm create --name myvm01 --resource-group myrs --admin-username admin --admin-password secure --image "OpenLogic:CentoOS:7.6:7.6.20190402" --subnet "/subscriptions/long-ass-name" --size Standard_B1ms
```

#### Common Commands

```powershell
# List PS version
$PSversionTable

# Logon to Azure (see above section too)
Login-AzAccount

# Get RBAC role definition(s)
$r = Get-AzRoleDefinition "Monitoring Contributor"
$r
$r | ? {$_.IsCustom -eq $true} | FT Name, IsCustom

# Get all role definitions in tenant and store as UTF8 text (makes easier Unix grep parsing, etc)
Get-AzRoleDefinition | ? {$_.IsCustom -eq $true} | ConvertTo-JSON | jq | Out-File -Encoding utf8 custom-roles.json

# Get/Select Specific Azure Subscription
Get-AzSubscription
Select-AzSubscription
Set-AzSubscription

# Update existing role
Get-AzRoleDefinition -Name "Existing Role" | ConvertTo-Json | Out-File existing-role.json
# Modify JSON file accordingly, then
Set-AzRoleDefinition -InputFile "existing-role.json"

# Create new custom role, based on existing
Get-AzRoleDefinition -Name "Existing Role" | ConvertTo-Json | Out-File azure-support-basic.json
# Modify JSON file accordingly, then
New-AzRoleDefinition -InputFile ./azure-support-basic.json

# Install YAML module
Install-Module -Name powershell-yaml -Force -Repository PSGallery -Scope CurrentUser
# Grab from file:
$r = Get-Content -Raw -Path file-path.json | ConvertFrom-Json
# Or query Azure
$r = Get-AzRoleDefinition "Monitoring Contributor"
$j = $r | ConvertTo-Json
$y = $r | ConvertTo-YAML

# Get existing role assignment (to then create one)
$a = Get-AzRoleAssignment [-RoleDefinitionName <String>] -Scope <String> | ConvertTo-Json 

# Create role assignment
$id = (Get-AzAdGroup -DisplayName MYGROUP).Id
New-AzRoleAssignment -RoleDefinition "azure-support-basic" -ObjectId $id

# Remove role
Get-AzureRmRoleDefinition -Name "Virtual Machine Operator" | Remove-AzureRmRoleDefinition

# Remove role assignment
$id = (Get-AzAdGroup -DisplayName MYGROUP).Id
Remove-AzRoleAssignment -ObjectId $id -RoleDefinitionName "azure-support-basic" 
```
